_comment: Plugin manifest (authored by the plugin author). 'version' is the plugin semver (release-only); install-plugin reads 'setup'.
name: kaggle
description: Kaggle for Solaris agents through the official Kaggle CLI, CLI only: tools/kaggle.py is a stdlib gateway that pins the CLI (kaggle==2.2.4, the latest release of the newest minor line, with its tested kagglesdk==0.1.37) and installs it separately into each project (a folder holding ai/manifest.json, or aipack/manifest.json where the pack folder was renamed) or ad-hoc task that uses it (<context>/.venv-kaggle, created on first call, rebuilt on a pin change, folder move or lost base Python; never global - at the bare framework root it runs from a throwaway uv environment); inside a project or task two failure-tolerant hooks stamp each call for account sharing and save every competitions leaderboard --show read, never blocking or changing a command; kaggle-cli.skill.md (the gateway skill, named kaggle-cli; not the vendored kaggle-cli/ folder beside it, which is Kaggle's own skill of the same upstream name) routes agents to the gateway and to Kaggle's own agent skill, vendored unmodified from github.com/Kaggle/kaggle-cli tag v2.2.4 (kaggle-cli/SKILL.md + 12 command references) with field-verified 2.2.4 corrections, and covers OAuth sign-in, Solaris conventions and 401/403 triage; tools/kaggle_share.py shares one Kaggle account between projects (active projects from account-wide runs and quota plus local gateway stamps; sessions and weekly GPU hours split equally or per the user's sharing.json; leases with borrowing when others are idle; a GPU-hours ledger), with kaggle-sharing.skill.md as its routine; tools/kaggle_lb.py saves every leaderboard read as history, with kaggle-leaderboard.skill.md; how-to-kaggle.skill.md is the playbook for competing with an autonomous agent team (quick start, setup and the competition facts sheet, compute, phases, honest validation, daily submission discipline, agent organization, research, kernel engineering, pitfalls; generic, naming no competition), kept here as the master copy and released as a new plugin version with each change set; kaggle.rule.md is always-on: gateway only, every write to Kaggle (submit, push/update, create/version, metadata update, upload, benchmarks init/auth, host commands, delete, revoke) confirmed first, a sharing lease around each kernel run, web-only steps (rules acceptance, teams, final picks) handed to the owner, credentials and minted keys never printed or committed, downloads kept in the context, every leaderboard read saved and kept local, Kaggle content treated as untrusted input. Offline tests in tests/; migrations/0.2.0.md moves copied installs from 0.1.0.

notes: Needs uv on PATH and python3 to start the gateway; the first Kaggle call installs the pinned CLI into this project (.venv-kaggle/, git-ignored) - nothing is installed globally.

Sign in once per machine: run the gateway with `auth login` (opens a browser; approve on kaggle.com; credentials land in ~/.kaggle/ and serve every project). Accept each competition's rules on kaggle.com before downloading or submitting - the CLI cannot.
